description: AFTER evidence, frame-time regression check, and final verification for WS3. Capture AFTER screenshots/sequences of the responsive camera moves, clickable interactions, and ambient life; measure AFTER Fast/High frame time per scene and prove Fast is NOT regressed vs the FEAT-001 BEFORE baseline; note any asset/byte added; confirm WS1/WS2 wins preserved; and record the final lint+build results. All evidence lands under docs/motion/.
steps: Ensure PATH has Node 22 and a fresh `npm run build` (static export in out/) reflecting FEAT-002 + FEAT-003 changes.

Capture AFTER fixed-camera screenshots + load JSON for chef, coach, pet, wardrobe routes into docs/motion/ using scripts/measure-load.mjs (labels after-chef, after-coach, after-pet, after-wardrobe). Where a single frame can't show motion, capture a short frame sequence or a couple of stills (idle vs mid-interaction) demonstrating the responsive camera + clickable interaction + ambient life.
Measure AFTER frame time for BOTH high and fast for each scene: node scripts/measure-frametime.mjs --dir out --route <route> --label after-<scene>-<quality> --out docs/motion --quality <high|fast>.

Write docs/motion/AFTER.md and docs/motion/DIFF.md: a table of BEFORE vs AFTER median frame time (Fast + High) per scene, explicitly showing Fast is not regressed (within noise on the SwiftShader software GL; state machine + browser). Explain that heavier ambient motion is High-only. If Fast regressed on any scene, treat it as a blocker and move the offending ambient motion behind High.

In AFTER.md, for EACH new interaction (chef click, coach click, pet click, wardrobe click, and each responsive camera move) document the exact code path proving it routes through the existing engine/state/content layer (click handler -> send()/doAction/setSelection -> respondToMessage/applyAction/OPTIONS -> response/state), and that the engines' behavior is unchanged.

Note any asset added and its size (expected: none — all procedural/in-memory), and confirm the WS1 cold-load byte budget is respected (compare after-*-load.json to the WS1/WS2 load numbers). Confirm WS1 wins (no re-eager preload, chunk split, useProgress fallback) and WS2 wins (shared High/Fast quality + lighting, single QualityToggle) are intact.
Run the final gate: `npm run lint` (font warning aside) and `npm run build` (all five routes prerender). Record both outputs in AFTER.md.
Stage ONLY source + docs/motion/ evidence; confirm out/, .next/, node_modules/, assets-src/ are not staged. Commit on motion/interactivity with a clear message. Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: docs/motion/ contains AFTER screenshots/sequences showing the responsive camera framing, the clickable interactions, and visible ambient life for all four affected scenes.
docs/motion/AFTER.md + DIFF.md show BEFORE vs AFTER Fast + High median frame time per scene with machine + browser, and demonstrate Fast is NOT regressed.
AFTER.md documents, per interaction, the code path proving routing through the existing engine/state/content layer, and confirms engine behavior is unchanged.
Any asset added is listed with size (expected none); WS1 byte budget respected; WS1 + WS2 wins confirmed preserved.
Final `npm run lint` (font warning aside) and `npm run build` pass; changes committed on motion/interactivity (not pushed); no build output / node_modules / assets-src committed.
verification: Re-run npm run lint && npm run build; confirm pass and all routes prerender.
Open the AFTER frame-time JSONs and confirm Fast median <= BEFORE Fast median within noise for every scene.
git status / git show --stat confirms only source + docs/motion/ are committed (no out/, .next/, node_modules/, assets-src/).
findings:
AFTER evidence + regression check + final verification done on branch motion/interactivity. Machine: Linux sandbox x86-64, software rasterizer ANGLE+SwiftShader. Browser: Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.10 (same build as the FEAT-001 BEFORE baseline). Node v22.23.2.

BUILD/LINT GATE (final): `npm run lint` clean except the single known @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning in app/layout.tsx (0 errors). `npm run build` (Next 16.2.11 Turbopack) static export succeeded; all five routes prerender static (/, /_not-found, /projects/chef-chatbot, /projects/coach-trainer, /projects/digital-wardrobe, /projects/virtual-pet). Recorded verbatim in docs/motion/AFTER.md.

FRAME TIME (Fast regression gate — THE load-bearing check): AFTER Fast median == BEFORE Fast median EXACTLY on every scene (Delta 0.0 ms): chef 66.7, coach 83.3, pet 183.3, wardrobe 83.3. High also flat: chef 83.3->83.3, coach 83.4->83.5 (+0.1 single-frame quantisation, not a regression), pet 283.3->283.3, wardrobe 116.7->116.7. NO Fast regression -> no need to move any ambient motion behind High as a fix (it was already gated High-only by FEAT-002/003). Per-scene JSON: docs/motion/after-<scene>-<fast|high>-frametime.json. Tables in AFTER.md + DIFF.md.

LOAD BYTES (WS1 budget): AFTER totals within a few KB of BEFORE (chef 2.605 vs 2.60 MB, coach 2.464 vs 2.46, pet 9.877 vs 9.87, wardrobe 8.271 vs 8.27) — code only, all ready:true, unresolvedFailures []. `git diff --stat 68adeb7..HEAD -- public/ assets-src/` is EMPTY => ZERO new assets (props + ambient all procedural / in-memory CanvasTexture). WS1 budget respected.

WS1/WS2 WINS PRESERVED (verified via git diff vs main 68adeb7): components/three/quality.ts, QualityToggle.tsx, SceneLoader.tsx and lib/pet/petState.ts are byte-UNCHANGED. No re-eager preload; scene code stays behind next/dynamic ssr:false; single shared QualityToggle is the only quality control; tone mapping stays ACESFilmic; no +/- on pinned framing lines (AIM_HEIGHT/CAMERA_DISTANCE/fov/MODEL_SCALE/AIM_MODEL_FRACTION/autoRotate).

EVIDENCE CAPTURED under docs/motion/ (committed): AFTER.md, DIFF.md, after-<scene>.png + .json (fixed-camera load), after-<scene>-<fast|high>-frametime.json, and idle-vs-mid-interaction stills after-<scene>-idle.png / after-<scene>-interact.png for all four scenes. The wardrobe pair visibly shows a garment change (orange tee -> hooded top) proving the torso click routes through cycleCategory('outfit')->setOption over OPTIONS; the pet pair shows the play push-in; chef/coach show the focus-driven camera nudge. Stills were captured with a THROWAWAY playwright-core driver (reused the committed harnesses' server + Chrome args; deleted after use, NOT committed) that drove the SAME real controls (suggestion chip / Play action button / canvas torso hit target) which exercise the identical engine/state/content input path a 3D prop click raises.

PER-INTERACTION ROUTING documented in AFTER.md citing real files/functions: chef SampleDishProp.onPointerDown -> ChefChatbot send('Suggest a recipe') -> respondToMessage (lib/chef/chefEngine.ts) -> reply+focus; coach KettlebellProp -> CoachChatbot send('Suggest a workout') -> respondToMessage (lib/coach/coachEngine.ts); pet <Pet> onPointerDown -> VirtualPet doAction('play') -> decayForElapsed+applyAction (lib/pet/petState.ts); wardrobe GarmentHitbox -> cycleCategory('outfit'/'bottom') -> setOption + nextIndex over OPTIONS (components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts). Every responsive camera move keys off the logic-layer output (focus / action+actionNonce / lastChange), never re-derived in the view; all layered additively over pinned framing via maath damp3/damp. Engines' reply/suggestions unchanged (FEAT-002 proved byte-identical); focus is additive only.

COMMIT: staged ONLY docs/motion/ evidence + the task-motion-interactivity FEAT-004/task state; out/, .next/, node_modules/, assets-src/ confirmed gitignored and NOT staged; unrelated .agents/tasks/* dirs left untracked (not part of this workstream). Did NOT push (orchestrator handles that).
